title: Sell Mineral Rights in Sylvania, PA
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Sylvania, PA
metaDescription: Own mineral rights near Sylvania in Bradford County? We buy dry-gas Marcellus interests directly from families and pay cash without pressure.
heroLead: Sylvania is a small crossroads community in Bradford County, and if the name makes you think of something else entirely, you're not alone. The gas history here is real and it runs deep, even if the town itself barely shows up on a map.
intro: Sylvania sits in rural Bradford County, in the dry-gas core of the Marcellus fairway where Chesapeake Energy and other operators built out extensive leasing positions during the 2008 to 2010 boom. Bradford County has consistently ranked among the most productive counties in the entire play, and family farms around Sylvania have often ended up inside large, multi-tract pooled units as a result.

A lot of Sylvania-area interests trace back to leases signed early in the boom, before landowners here had much bargaining leverage or legal guidance, which means post-production deduction language on these older leases is often less favorable than what a family would negotiate today.

sections.heading: Rural Farm Tracts in a Heavily Pooled Area
paragraphs: Units around Sylvania frequently pull acreage from several adjoining farms, which means your royalty is calculated based on your proportionate share of the unit rather than just what sits directly under your own property. Confirming that percentage accurately is one of the first things we do.

sections.heading: Reading an Older Bradford County Lease Honestly
paragraphs: If your lease was signed during the initial boom years, gathering and compression deductions permitted under Kilmer v. Elexco may be reducing your net royalty well below the one-eighth minimum's headline value. We review your specific lease terms and explain exactly what's happening on your statement.

faqs.question: How do I confirm my percentage share of a pooled unit near Sylvania?
faqs.answer: Your division order should list your unit participation percentage. We can also verify this against DEP pooling orders on file for your specific unit.

faqs.question: Is my land still producing after all these years?
faqs.answer: Many Bradford County wells drilled during the original boom continue producing steadily, though at declining rates over time. We check current production data for your specific unit.

faqs.question: What if I never signed a lease at all?
faqs.answer: Unleased minerals in an active area like this still carry value. We can evaluate an unleased interest and explain how that differs from a producing, leased one.

faqs.question: How do you value a fractional interest split among several family members?
faqs.answer: We confirm your exact percentage against the recorder of deeds records, then value your share based on the unit's production and your specific fraction, not the tract as a whole.
